answer: Stake-weighted reputation makes each fake identity expensive: joining requires locking a deposit, so a thousand sock puppets means a thousand deposits, a cost scaling linearly with the attack. Honest work unlocks the deposit and builds a public history, like layers of shale pressed into a durable record, while misbehavior triggers slashing that burns part of the stake. Peers mirror each other's attestations, cross-checking a newcomer before trusting it, so one fake identity cannot manufacture credibility alone. The deposit is a signal, not a fee: proof the agent has something real to lose.
